default_scope: SHAKE requests in the imported-component GPU aggregation runner run command. N4 uses up to 16 native proofs per batch; N3 retains its four-native/32 GiB envelope. Historical profiling commands and explicit machine comparison remain available.
implemented: Typed request proofs bind exact request descriptor, index, context, statement, endpoints and complete coverage in existing graph consumers.
One weighted CPU preparation queue spans SHAKE requests and transactions, with up to 16 workers and one GPU owner. Native and symbolic preparation reservations are included.
GPU proving state retains compact AIR descriptors; compiler source is retired before private GPU work, releasing the weighted permit for another preparation job.
One exact-identity public preprocessing cache occupies the existing backend allowance. A miss evicts before replacement; no compiler programs, witnesses or private randomizers are cached.
Matching request positions are adjacent across transactions, and parent reductions follow request order, to improve exact-template reuse.
AES, graph/final proof encoding and v1 verification remain on their existing routes; typed SHAKE proofs are constrained through the request bridge.

memory.note: Existing exclusive zero-swap guard and device allocation checks retained. Public cache has one entry within the backend partition.

planning.note: Descriptor planning only; this is not a measured full N4 speedup.

comparison.note: Same deterministic N4 archive/request 6. Native preparation and independent CPU verification are included. New warm timings retain public preprocessing; prior R75 recreated it each sample.

scope_limits: Only complete SHAKE request 6 was timed. The 1-versus-16 worker comparison uses three four-native-or-smaller batches and one parent; only three preparation jobs are available.
More preparation workers did not reduce latency in that bounded comparison; no larger-workload worker speedup is claimed.
Cold default request remains above 20 seconds. Full 109-component, N3 and N4 runtime targets remain unmeasured.
The direct typed transcript/Merkle/FRI frontend, typed AES/graph/final execution and standalone AggregateArtifactV2 remain outstanding.
